Trader consensus, reflected in the 72.5% implied probability for 33°C, centers on the upper end of this forecast envelope, while lower probabilities for 32°C and 34°C capture residual uncertainty in exact peak timing and local measurement. Updated model runs and surface observations through the day will refine resolution criteria.

Ensemble model spreads reflect modest uncertainty around steering patterns and timing of any rain bands, supporting the tight clustering between 28°C and 30°C rather than a dominant single outcome.

**Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble models indicate a high near 75–77°F for New York City on August 22, 2026, driven by persistent easterly flow, cloud cover, and scattered shower activity that limits daytime heating.** 

This pattern features an onshore component off the Atlantic, promoting marine-layer influence and reduced solar insolation compared with typical late-summer conditions. Seasonal averages for Central Park highs hover around 83°F, yet current model runs show suppressed maxima due to overcast skies and isolated thunderstorms, keeping surface temperatures several degrees cooler. 

Traders have priced this consensus into the market, with 76–77°F holding the largest share of implied probability at 45.5% and the adjacent 74–75°F and 78–79°F bins capturing most of the remainder. Shifts in the latest model guidance—particularly any reduction in cloud cover or earlier clearing—could nudge outcomes slightly higher, while heavier or more persistent precipitation would reinforce the lower side of the range. Resolution depends on the official highest reading recorded at the designated NYC station.
